title: Oil prices hit $100 for the first time since May
facts: Brent crude oil prices surpassed $100 per barrel on Thursday for the first time since May.
Brent crude oil prices increased by more than 6% on Thursday following several consecutive days of price gains.
Houthi militia in Yemen attacked oil tankers in the Red Sea.
The benchmark UK gas price reached approximately 150p per therm, rising from around 98p at the end of June.
The United States and Israel began military action against Iran on February 28.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the leaders in Iran were not ready to make a deal.
The UK annual inflation rate fell to 2.6% in the year to June.
The United States annual inflation rate stood at 3.5%.
UK petrol prices increased by 5p per litre since early July to reach nearly £1.56.
Diesel prices in the UK reached an average of £1.72 per litre according to the RAC.
Average gasoline prices in the United States surpassed $4.00 per gallon according to AAA.
Average US gasoline prices were $3.92 per gallon one month prior.
The Bank of England maintained UK interest rates at 3.75% across four consecutive meetings.
Kevin Warsh was newly appointed as the chair of the US Federal Reserve.
The US Federal Reserve held interest rates between 3.5% and 3.75% during Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair.
